CausalChain: Metabolic stress -> Overexpression of MALAT1 -> MALAT1 conformation change to a stable triple helix (enhanced by adaptor proteins, validated by cryo-EM and crosslinking-MS) -> Conditional scaffold formation recruiting glycolytic enzymes and integrating with gene regulatory networks (mapped by CLIP-seq) -> Enhanced local glycolytic activity and metabolic plasticity -> Tumor metabolic reprogramming -> Disruption of the triple helix by structure-based small molecules (informed by AI-driven modelling) -> Inhibition of enzyme recruitment and regulatory interactions -> Reversal of stress-induced metabolic adaptations -> Reduced tumor progression
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in response to metabolic stress, cancer cells overexpress the long noncoding RNA MALAT1 which, through stress-induced signals, folds into a highly stable triple helix structure. This structure, further stabilized by specific RNA-binding adaptor proteins, acts as a conditional scaffold that spatially organizes key glycolytic enzymes through both direct binding and adaptor-mediated interactions. Simultaneously, the MALAT1 triple helix modulates gene regulatory networks pivotal to metabolic adaptation. Utilizing contemporary technologies—such as AI-driven RNA structure predictions, high-resolution cryo-EM imaging to resolve the molecular structure, CLIP-seq to identify RNA-protein interacting domains, CRISPR-based targeted modifications, and single-cell metabolomic profiling—we will verify this molecular assembly. Moreover, we propose that structure-based small molecules can be rationally designed to selectively disrupt the triple helix structure of MALAT1. This disruption is anticipated to disassemble the localized glycolytic enzyme complexes and abrogate the associated gene regulatory interactions, thereby reversing the metabolic reprogramming specific to tumor cells while leaving the metabolism of normal tissues largely intact.
Abstract: This study proposes that under metabolic stress, cancer cells upregulate MALAT1, which subsequently adopts a highly stable triple helix conformation. This conformational change, enhanced by specific RNA-binding adaptor proteins, functions as a conditional molecular scaffold that spatially orchestrates the assembly of key glycolytic enzymes and integrates critical gene regulatory networks. Such scaffolding localizes metabolic flux and promotes metabolic plasticity, fueling tumor progression. By leveraging advanced technologies – including AI-driven RNA structure prediction, high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), CLIP-seq for RNA-protein interaction mapping, CRISPR-based genome editing, and single-cell metabolomics – we will characterize the molecular interfaces and dynamic interactions of the MALAT1 triple helix. Furthermore, we hypothesize that precise structure-based small molecules can disrupt the MALAT1 triple helix, thereby impairing enzyme recruitment and regulatory interactions. This targeted disruption is expected to selectively reverse the adaptive metabolic reprogramming of tumor cells while sparing normal tissues, providing a novel therapeutic avenue in metabolically demanding oncogenic environments.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis posited that MALAT1 forms a triple helix structure under metabolic stress to orchestrate glycolytic enzyme assembly and gene regulation, with potential therapeutic disruption using small molecules. In the revised hypothesis, we have refined and expanded the causal chain by explicitly incorporating advanced technological capabilities such as AI-driven RNA structure prediction, cryo-EM, and CLIP-seq for detailed mapping of RNA-protein interactions. We clarified the dual scaffold and gene regulatory roles of the triple helix, provided a more detailed and testable mechanism for its formation and function under stress, and outlined integrative validation strategies (including CRISPR perturbation and single-cell metabolomics) to ensure selective disruption of tumor metabolism. This renders the hypothesis not only more specific and mechanistically detailed but also enhances its practical implementability.
